338976.title: Sublattice conjecture for c-Cambrian order interval posets
338976.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be a finite root system, let $c$ be a Coxeter element, and let $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)$ be the poset of $\Phi$-posets equipped with its weak order. Let $\mathsf{COIP}(c)$ be the set of $c$-Cambrian order interval posets.

**Sublattice conjecture for c-Cambrian order interval posets.** For every Coxeter element $c$, the set $\mathsf{COIP}(c)$ induces a sublattice of the weak order on $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)$.

The source explicitly states that this conjecture remains open, although it was proved in type $A$ and verified for small Coxeter types by computation. It is not implied by the established sublattice result inside the weak-order posets because those posets do not themselves form a sublattice of $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)$.

339805.title: Zerbini's single-valued multiple zeta value conjecture for modular graph functions
339805.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph, and let

$$
D_{\Gamma}(\tau)=\sum_{k=1-l}^l\,\sum_{m,n\geq 0}d_k^{(m,n)}(\Gamma)\,y^kq^m\overline{q}^n
$$

be its modular graph function, with $l$ edges, $q=\exp(2\pi i\tau)$, and $y=\pi\,\operatorname{Im}(\tau)$. Denote by $\mathcal{Z}^{\rm sv}$ the algebra of single-valued multiple zeta values. **Zerbini's conjecture.** The coefficients $d_k^{(m,n)}(\Gamma)$ belong to $\mathcal{Z}^{\rm sv}$. Explicit computations support this assertion, including cases where higher-depth multiple zeta values occur; the conjecture remains open for arbitrary modular graph functions.

340118.title: The arbitrary-boundary network decomposition conjecture
340118.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a network with $n\geq2$ boundary vertices. An **extremal-ray realization** is a subnetwork whose entropy vector realizes an extremal ray of the $n$-boundary-region holographic entropy cone. **The arbitrary-boundary network decomposition conjecture.** A network with $n\geq2$ boundary vertices decomposes into subnetworks, each of which is an extremal-ray realization of the $n$-boundary-region holographic entropy cone. This generalizes the proposed four-partite network decomposition; the source reports numerical evidence for the four-boundary case, while no general proof is given.

340831.title: The tree cover bound for connected triangle-free graphs
340831.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices, and let $T(G)$ denote its tree cover number.

**Triangle-free tree cover conjecture.** For all connected triangle-free graphs,

$$
T(G)\leq\left\lceil\frac{n}{3}\right\rceil.
$$

The question arises because a related bound for graphs of girth at least five does not extend to the four-cycle; the conjecture is motivated by computations in Sage and remains open in the supplied source.

341273.title: Reducibility reformulation of McDiarmid–Reed's conjecture
341273.statement:
Let $G$ be a hexagonal graph, and let $\mathcal{F}_{9,4}$ and $\mathcal{F}'_{9,4}$ be the families of $(9,4)$-reducible H-handles used in the paper. Write $\operatorname{core}_{\mathcal{F}_{9,4}\cup\mathcal{F}'_{9,4}}(G)$ for the graph obtained after reducing $G$ by these configurations.

**McDiarmid–Reed reducibility conjecture.** For every hexagonal graph $G$, $\operatorname{core}_{\mathcal{F}_{9,4}\cup\mathcal{F}'_{9,4}}(G)$ is $(9,4)$-colorable.

The statement is presented as an equivalent form of McDiarmid–Reed's conjecture. The paper's new reductions substantially decrease the number of irreducible configurations found computationally, but some configurations remain and no proof is given.

341963.title: The polynomial-size DFJ relaxation conjecture for cubic graphs
341963.statement:
Let $amma$ be a cubic graph. Let $
Mathcal{P}_b$ be the feasible region defined by constraints $$--$$, and let $
Mathcal{P}_c$ be the feasible region defined by the degree, subtour, symmetry, upper-bound, and nonnegativity constraints $$--$$, where $S$ ranges over proper subsets of the vertices of $amma$. **Polynomial-size DFJ relaxation conjecture.** The constraints $$--$$ form a polynomial-size set equivalent to the exponential-size set $$--$$; equivalently, $\mathcal{P}_b=\mathcal{P}_c$. If true, this would provide a polynomial-size description of the DFJ feasible region for every cubic graph. The claim is motivated only by computational comparisons in the source, which reports that the two formulations identified exactly the same tested non-Hamiltonian graphs; no resolution is given.

342196.title: Equality of the Fibonacci gap sets
342196.statement:
Let $D_\ell$ and $U_\ell$ be the down-gap and up-gap sets, respectively, defined by

$$
D_\ell=\{d_{k+\ell}-d_k:k\geq 1\},
$$

with $U_\ell$ defined analogously. **Equality of the Fibonacci gap sets.** For every positive integer $\ell$,

$$
D_\ell=U_\ell.
$$

The equality is known for $\ell=1$ and $\ell=2$, but the general case is posed as an open problem and is motivated by computations and the techniques used to establish results for small gap lengths.

342250.title: Nonvanishing conjecture for symmetric Wigner 6j symbols
342250.statement:
Let $k,n$ be integers and let

$$
\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}k&k&k\\frac n2&\frac n2&\frac n2\end{array}\right\}
$$

be the Wigner $6j$ symbol appearing in the description of the cubic invariant $\mathscr{P}_{n,3}(F)$. **Nonvanishing conjecture.** For every pair of integers $(k,n)$ with $n\ge k\ge2$, except $(k,n)=(2,3)$, one has

$$
\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}k&k&k\\frac n2&\frac n2&\frac n2\end{array}\right\}\ne0.
$$

The claim is a purely combinatorial conjecture motivated by computer checks and by the proposed regular-sequence extension of Dixmier's conjecture; the source does not state that it has been proved or disproved.

342320.title: Boldt–Lauret–Schüth conjecture on Dirac-isospectral spin lens spaces
342320.statement:
Let two spin lens spaces have dimension $d$ satisfying

$$
d\equiv 1\pmod 4.
$$

**Boldt–Lauret–Schüth conjecture.** If the two spin lens spaces are Dirac isospectral, then they are isometric. The claim is supported by computational evidence for spin lens spaces, while the supplied source notes that it fails for arbitrary spin manifolds because Dirac-isospectral nonisometric compact flat manifolds exist.

342367.title: The conjectures on valuations for non-prime-power colored partition functions
342367.statement:
Let $S_{k,m}(n)$ be the $n$th coefficient in the power-series expansion defining the $m$-colored $k$-ary partition function, and let 
$$
\varphi_k(n)=\max\{s\in\mathbb{N}:k^s\mid n\},\qquad \varphi_k(0)=+\infty.
$$
 **Non-prime-power valuation conjectures.** If $k$ is not a power of a prime number, then for every $m\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, the sequence $(\varphi_k(S_{k,m}(n)))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is unbounded and is not $k$-regular. These claims are based on numerical computations and remain open.

342879.title: Conjecture on Gallai–Ramsey numbers of even wheels
342879.statement:
Let $W_{2n}$ denote the wheel graph with an even cycle of length $2n$, let $GR_k(H)$ denote the $k$-color Gallai–Ramsey number of a graph $H$, and let $R_2(W_{2n})$ denote the two-color Ramsey number of $W_{2n}$. **Even-wheel Gallai–Ramsey conjecture.** For all $k\ge2$ and $n\ge2$, 

$$
GR_k(W_{2n})=\begin{cases}(R_2(W_{2n})-1)\cdot5^{\frac{k-2}{2}}+1,&\text{if }k\text{ is even},\\2(R_2(W_{2n})-1)\cdot5^{\frac{k-3}{2}}+1,&\text{if }k\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

The formula is motivated by the exact computation of $GR_k(W_4)$ for all $k\ge2$, together with a lower bound for general even wheels. Its validity for all even wheels and all $k\ge2$ remains open.

342973.title: Existence of strong signed edge-labelings in 3-connected planar graphs
342973.statement:
Let $H$ be a 3-connected planar graph with an even number of negative vertices. A $\{0,a,b\}$-edge-labeling $c$ is a **strong signed edge-labeling** if it is a weak signed edge-labeling and

$$
d_0(v)<d_H(v)
$$

for every odd-degree vertex $v$ of $H$. **Strong signed edge-labeling existence claim.** There exists a strong signed edge-labeling of $H$.

This strengthens the preceding weak-labeling assertion and is used in the paper's structural analysis of signed planar graphs. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, and the claim's precise status should be checked against the paper's proof.

343264.title: Extremal critical-point conjecture for quadrature domains
343264.statement:
Let an **RL-domain** be a domain of order $n$ and connectivity $k$ whose landscape function is defined as in the paper. For integers $n\geq 2$ and $1\leq k\leq n+1$, the conjecture is that there exists an RL-domain $\Omega$ of order $n$ and connectivity $k$ whose landscape function has exactly

$$
4n+k-6
$$

critical points in $\Omega$.

**Extremal critical-point conjecture.** For every $n\geq 2$, and for each $k=1,2,\ldots,n+1$, such a domain exists. The bound is attained for $k=n+1$ by the extremal construction described in the paper; existence for all connectivities is supported by computer simulations but remains unproved.

344036.title: The involution-word bumping conjecture for queer supercrystals
344036.statement:
Let $I_\mathbb{Z}$ denote the set of involutions in the infinite symmetric group, let $w=w_1w_2\cdots w_n$ be an involution word, and let $\mathfrak{ib}_\pi$ be the involution-word bumping operator. Suppose

$$
\mathfrak{ib}_\pi(w)=\tilde w_1\tilde w_2\cdots\tilde w_n.
$$

**Involution-word bumping conjecture.** For every $i\in[n]$, one has $\tilde w_i-w_i\in\{0,1\}$.

Computations support this analogue of the corresponding result for Edelman–Greene insertion; if true, it would immediately prove the most difficult part of the stated theorem on the orthogonal insertion algorithm. The conjecture is presented as open in the source.

344167.title: The Genocchi cycle-counting conjecture
344167.statement:
A **drop** of a permutation or cycle on a finite set of positive integers is a pair $(i,\sigma(i))$ with $i>\sigma(i)$; it is an **even-odd drop** when $i$ is even and $\sigma(i)$ is odd. Let $g_n$ denote the Genocchi numbers.

**Genocchi cycle-counting conjecture.** For all $n\geq 1$, $g_n$ is equal to the number of cycles on $[2n]$ with only even-odd drops.

This gives a combinatorial formula for the Genocchi numbers analogous to the stated formula for the median Genocchi numbers. The conjecture was verified by computer for $n\leq 6$, but no general proof or resolution is supplied here.

345077.title: Three odd Gaussian primes conjecture for the first quadrant
345077.statement: Let $A=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}[i]\mid\operatorname{Re}(z)>0\text{ and }\operatorname{Im}(z)>0\}$, and let $K_\pi=\{z\in\pi_{\mathbb{Z}[i]}\mid\operatorname{Re}(z)\geq0\text{ and }\operatorname{Im}(z)\geq0\}$. **Three odd Gaussian primes conjecture.** For every $z\in A$ with $\max(\operatorname{Re}(z),\operatorname{Im}(z))\geq7$, the Gaussian integer $z$ is a sum of at most three odd primes from $K_\pi$. This is motivated by computational experiments on representations of Gaussian integers; the source gives no proof or resolution.

365404.title: Monotonicity conjecture for hook counts in t-regular partitions
365404.statement:
For integers $t\geq2$ and $k\geq1$, let $b_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of hooks of length $k$ in all $t$-regular partitions of $n$. A $t$-regular partition is a partition with no part divisible by $t$.

**Monotonicity conjecture.** Let $t\geq3$ be an integer. Then

$$
b_{t+1,2}(n)\geq b_{t,2}(n),
$$

for all $n\geq0$.

The conjecture formalizes numerical evidence that the number of hooks of length $2$ in $t$-regular partitions increases with $t$. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

373925.title: Rear-central nucleation conjecture for higher simplicial behaviour in the partition graph
373925.statement: Let $G_n$ be the partition graph on the partitions associated with the parameter $n$, and consider its simplicial thick zones, including the tetrahedral and higher-order regions. The front extremes and antennas refer to the frontal extremal parts of the graph, while the rear-central part and central rear body refer to the corresponding geometric regions described by the shell/core structure. **Rear-central nucleation conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, the first genuinely higher simplicial behaviour of the partition graph is nucleated in the rear-central part of $G_n$. Equivalently, the earliest tetrahedral and higher-order thick zones are asymptotically separated from the front extremes and are organized around the central rear body of the graph rather than around its antennas. This strengthens the observed fact that substantial thickening begins in a rear-central region rather than at the front. Computational examples suggest a relationship with the self-conjugate axis and the spine, but the claim does not assert that maximal-thickness vertices lie on the axis, remain at bounded distance from the spine, or that higher-dimensional thick regions are connected or unique.

375034.title: Bsila–Cox–Hugo–Styron–Zhuang fixed–pixed points equidistribution conjecture
375034.statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be the family

$$
\mathcal P=
\left\{
\begin{array}{ccc}
\{132,312\}, & \{132,321\}, & \{213,231\},\\[2mm]
\{123,132,312\}, & \{123,213,231\}, & \{123,312,321\},\\[2mm]
\{132,312,321\}, & \{213,231,312\}, & \{213,231,321\}
\end{array}
\right\}.
$$

For $\Pi\in\mathcal P$, let $\mathfrak S_n(\Pi)$ denote the permutations of length $n$ avoiding every pattern in $\Pi$, and let $\operatorname{fix}$ and $\operatorname{pix}$ be the fixed-point and pixed-point statistics, respectively. **Bsila–Cox–Hugo–Styron–Zhuang conjecture.** For all $n\geq 0$ and every $\Pi\in\mathcal P$, the statistics $\operatorname{fix}$ and $\operatorname{pix}$ are equidistributed over $\mathfrak S_n(\Pi)$. Equivalently,

$$
\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n(\Pi)} x^{\operatorname{fix}(\pi)}=\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n(\Pi)} x^{\operatorname{pix}(\pi)}.
$$

The conjecture concerns a common refinement of enumeration for restricted permutations and desarrangements. The source notes that Zhuang and his students independently obtained a bijective proof of the original conjecture, so the status of this formulation should be checked against that result.

381433.title: Cardoso–Luz conjecture on adverse graphs
381433.statement:
An **adverse graph** is a graph $H$ without isolated vertices such that $upsilon(H)$ and $lambda_{min}(H)$ are integers, and, for every vertex $i\in V(H)$,

$$
\upsilon(H-N_H(i))=\upsilon(H),\qquad \lambda_{min}(H-N_H(i))=\lambda_{min}(H).
$$

Here $upsilon(H)$ is the optimal value of the quadratic stability-number bound and $lambda_{min}(H)$ is the least eigenvalue of $H$. A graph is a **$\mathcal{Q}$-graph** when it belongs to the class $\mathcal{Q}$ defined in the paper.

**Cardoso–Luz conjecture.** All adverse graphs are $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.

Computational tests with adverse graphs supported the conjecture, but it remains open. Its resolution would clarify the polynomial-time recognition of $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.
